ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the line $y=-\frac{2}{3}x+2$ intersects the x-axis at point A and the y-axis at point B. The parabola $y=-\frac{2}{3}x^2+bx+c$ passes through points A and B. What is the expression of this parabola?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From $y=-\frac{2}{3}x+2$, we obtain:\\
When $x=0$, $y=2$; when $y=0$, $x=3$,\\
$\therefore \boxed{A(3,0)}, \boxed{B(0,2)}$,\\
Substituting the coordinates of $A$, $B$ into $y=-\frac{2}{3}x^{2}+bx+c$ yields:\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
-\frac{2}{3}\times 9+3b+c=0 \\
c=2
\end{array}\right.$,\\
Solving this gives: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}
b=\frac{4}{3} \\
c=2
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore$ The equation of the parabola is: \boxed{y=-\frac{2}{3}x^{2}+\frac{4}{3}x+2}.
